studies.label: FIERO versus Google Docs collaborative superhero-story writing

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 13, Section 4.1 (random assignment); PDF p. 41, Table 1 caption and note (questionnaire arm and total counts)
counts_source.quote: In this between-subjects experiment, 60 participants were randomly assigned to either a story creation group or a card game-based story creation group. ... (n=30 per group) ... (N=60).

arms.name: FIERO
arms.description: Face-to-face collaborative writing with physical narrative cards, a shared FIERO interface, generated images, optional AI decision support, and final-story suggestions and polishing. The analyzed count is the questionnaire count (PDF p. 41, Table 1); people represented by the scored-story corpus are not identified. Arm-specific randomization counts are not separately reported.

arms.name: Control (Google Docs)
arms.description: Face-to-face collaborators draft, discuss, and integrate a superhero story in a shared Google Docs document, following the same narrative tasks and round timing. No AI or physical cards. The analyzed count is the questionnaire count (PDF p. 41, Table 1); people represented by the scored-story corpus are not identified. Arm-specific randomization counts are not separately reported.

studies.task: Teams of three collaboratively write a superhero story through hero, villain/scene, and weapon/climax rounds, then integrate the final narrative (PDF pp. 13-14, Section 4.1; PDF pp. 47-48, Appendix E).

ai_tool.name: FIERO: GPT-4 for decision support and final-story assistance; GPT-4o image model (gpt-4o-image) for images
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 12, Section 3.4; PDF p. 49, Appendix F.1, Table 5. Model release year is not printed.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Claude Opus 4.5. Creativity assesses originality, innovative concepts, uniqueness, fresh perspectives, and imaginative content (PDF pp. 15-16; Appendix D, PDF p. 46). Pairwise LLM judgment of the final team-authored stories, using the same rubric for all judges. Each of nine FIERO texts is compared with each of nine control texts in both AB and BA order; inconsistent directional judgments become draws (PDF p. 17, Section 4.5.2). Judges evaluate the same story corpus; they are measurement variants, not independent samples.

stats.difference_is: As printed: percentage net advantage of FIERO over control in pairwise judgments; FIERO win percentage minus control win percentage. Kept in the printed percentage units.

estimates.notes: The analyzed people counts are not reported for the scored-story corpus. The study and arm analyzed counts describe questionnaires, not this outcome. sources.locator: PDF p. 27, Section 5.4.1, overall comparison chi-squared test

estimates.notes: The analyzed people counts are not reported for the scored-story corpus. The study and arm analyzed counts describe questionnaires, not this outcome. The comparison denominator is printed in the overall win fractions (PDF p. 27); the common pairwise protocol applies across dimensions (PDF pp. 17 and 27). FIERO combines AI with cards and gameplay; the contrast does not isolate AI. treatment_mean is the printed FIERO win percentage, not a continuous participant-level story score. The printed win fraction is preserved in its source quote. Control win percentages and judge-specific draw percentages are available only in the Figure 13 graphic and are not transcribed under extraction Rule 1. The prose reports only the range of draw percentages across judges. No difference is computed. Degrees of freedom are not printed; the superscript in chi-squared is not a degree of freedom. The reported test uses repeated story-pair comparisons and describes no participant, team, or story adjustment. No SE, confidence interval, or standardized effect is reported. Section 5.4.1/Figure 13 and the Overall row in Section 5.4.2/Figure 14 are retained as separate summaries of the same sample and form outcome. Appendix D prints both Overall and Final_Winner fields (PDF p. 47), without mapping them to the summaries. They must not be merged or treated as independent outcomes; the Claude summaries do not reconcile as the same win-minus-loss measure.

open_items: The number of analyzed people for story outcomes is not printed. PDF p. 16, Section 4.4, reports 30 recruited people and ten teams per arm, whereas PDF p. 17, Section 4.5.2, analyzes nine texts per arm. The omitted texts/teams and any corresponding participant exclusions are not identified; no participant count is inferred by multiplying texts by team size.

PDF p. 13, Section 4.1, explicitly states random assignment of participants, but does not describe the allocation procedure or whether teams formed before or after allocation. The paper does not establish the number or treatment composition of distinct experimental sessions sufficiently to replace the stated individual assignment unit.

The relationship between Section 5.4.1/Figure 13 overall comparisons and Section 5.4.2/Figure 14 Overall Preference is unresolved. Appendix D (PDF p. 47) has Overall and Final_Winner fields but does not map them to the reported summaries. The Claude summaries are inconsistent if interpreted as the same win-minus-loss measure.

No participant-, team-, or story-adjusted SEs or confidence intervals are reported for the scored-story outcomes. The printed chi-squared tests concern repeated story-pair comparisons, with no reported dependence adjustment or degrees of freedom (PDF p. 27). No usable outcome SDs or standardized effects are supplied.

Numerical text or tables are needed for the control win percentages and judge-specific draw percentages in Figure 13, and for the dimension-by-judge values in Figure 14 that the prose or caption does not explicitly identify. Those figure-only numbers remain unrecorded under extraction Rule 1; ranges across judges are not CIs.
Country of data collection and release year of the specific assistance models are not stated in the paper. Author affiliations and template publication dates are not used to infer them.
notes: Extraction B, completed from the saved PDF. The full markdown conversion was read in consecutive chunks, including references and Appendices A-H; all cited numerical passages were checked using pymupdf. The PDF tables, figures, and appendices were inspected before the design and methods. The study-level analyzed count and arm counts are explicitly the questionnaire sample. PDF p. 16, Section 4.4, reports ten three-person teams per arm; these are not coded as confirmed randomized clusters because the stated assignment is of individuals and team-formation timing is unknown. Participants were non-professional creators recruited by word of mouth and social media, including students and non-students; the country is unstated (PDF p. 16). The AI role is other because the intervention combines image generation, decision support, and refinement (PDF p. 12 and Appendix F). Both arms already include human collaboration, so the comparison is ai_vs_bau. The authors explicitly acknowledge the bundled intervention (PDF p. 34, Section 6.6.1). Outcome inventory: Creativity, Overall Preference, Plot Coherence, Development, Language Use, Anthropomorphism, and Character Fidelity, each evaluated by Claude Opus 4.5, Gemini 3 Pro, and GPT-5.2; the additional overall-comparison summaries remain distinct from the Overall Preference dimension. All printed inferential story-outcome statistics are the overall chi-squared tests in Section 5.4.1. Net advantages have no reported uncertainty. The numeric net advantages retained come from the Figure 14 caption for Creativity and the Section 5.4.2 prose for Gemini Development and Anthropomorphism. No number was estimated or transcribed solely from a graphic, and no difference, SD, SE, CI, or effect size was computed. Null-valued eligible contrasts remain in estimates with textual evidence and explanatory notes. Model judgments are measurements of human-produced work, not model-only experimental arms. No eligible across_people or after_ai outcome is reported; remarks about homogenization are qualitative. No sample overlap is identified in the reconciled screening form. Appendix H identifies system, card, and prompt artifacts, but no separate participant/story dataset (PDF p. 51).
